title: Outlive
author: Peter Attia

lessons.title: Plan for Your Marginal Decade
lessons.key_idea: Your last decade of life is often spent in decline, and the real goal is to extend healthspan, the years you live with a capable body and mind, not just lifespan.
issues: scene 4: The 'INDEPENDENCE' label overflows the amber puzzle piece. Its first letters run into the left knob cut-out and touch the piece outline, so text overlaps the shape edge. (fix: Shrink the label or widen the piece, then centre the text inside the solid body of the piece with at least 16px padding from the knob cut-outs. Alternatively, place the label below the piece.)

scene 0: The 'OR' label between the two figures is tiny, well under 18px at 1600 width. The two figures are also small and hard to read: the hiking figure's pole reads as a walking cane. (fix: Enlarge the figures by about 1.5x. Raise the 'OR' label to at least 20px. Make the active figure clearly hiking, e.g. mid-stride with a backpack, instead of standing with a cane-like stick.)

lessons.title: From Medicine 2.0 to 3.0
lessons.key_idea: Standard medicine waits for disease to appear and then treats it, while Attia's Medicine 3.0 aims to prevent illness early with care tailored to each person.

lessons.title: Meet the Four Horsemen
lessons.key_idea: Heart disease, cancer, neurodegenerative disease and metabolic dysfunction cause most deaths, develop silently over decades, and must be tackled long before symptoms appear.

lessons.title: Exercise Is the Strongest Longevity Drug
lessons.key_idea: Aerobic fitness, built through steady Zone 2 training and pushing up your VO2 max, is one of the strongest predictors of how long and how well you live.

lessons.title: Train for Your Centenarian Decathlon
lessons.key_idea: Choose the physical tasks you want to do in your last decade, like lifting a grandchild or climbing stairs, then build the strength and stability now to still do them later.

lessons.title: Eat and Sleep with Purpose
lessons.key_idea: No single diet suits everyone, so adjust what you eat to your own body, with enough protein to protect muscle, and treat sleep as a pillar of health.

lessons.title: Emotional Health Makes It Worthwhile
lessons.key_idea: Attia's own struggle taught him that a longer life means little without emotional well-being, which deserves the same deliberate effort as body and brain.

plan.title: Outlive
plan.author: Peter Attia, with Bill Gifford
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's main frameworks and arguments well, but not every specific anecdote or figure, so lessons should stick to its core concepts.
plan.one_liner: Living longer is not enough. Here is how to stay strong, sharp and happy into your final decade.
plan.summary: Physician Peter Attia argues that modern medicine is good at treating acute illness but too slow to prevent the chronic diseases that actually kill most of us. He calls these the Four Horsemen: heart disease, cancer, neurodegenerative disease like Alzheimer's, and metabolic dysfunction such as type 2 diabetes. Each one builds silently for decades, so he urges a proactive, personalized approach he calls Medicine 3.0. The goal is not just more years but better ones, extending healthspan as well as lifespan. His most powerful tool is exercise, including aerobic fitness, strength and stability, trained deliberately for the life you want at 90. He adds nutrition, sleep and, finally, emotional health, drawing on his own painful journey to show that longevity matters only if the life is worth living.
